records.label: Wa ceasefire administration
records.relationship: A separate armed administration under a ceasefire relationship. It is not part of the military chain of command and should not be treated as a branch of the NUG/PDF resistance.
records.note: The northern and southern territories are separate. Southern Wa territory lies outside the formal Wa Self-Administered Division. Wa remains within Myanmar; this is not an internationally recognised country.
records.asOf: Reference territory · effective boundary date unspecified
records.source: IISS Myanmar Conflict Map · retrieved 18 October 2026

records.label: Mongla ceasefire administration
records.relationship: A separate ceasefire administration in eastern Shan State, distinct from Wa, the central military authorities and the NUG/PDF resistance.
records.note: Mongla is the NDAA headquarters. A ceasefire relationship is different from direct rule by the military.
records.asOf: Reference territory · effective boundary date unspecified
records.source: IISS Myanmar Conflict Map · retrieved 18 October 2026

military.name: Naypyitaw
military.note: Seat of the military-backed national authorities. A point showing a governing centre, not a polygon of surrounding military control.

military.name: Yangon
military.note: Reported military-controlled urban centre. Resistance activity can occur inside cities; this marker does not assign its whole township or region to one side.

military.name: Mandalay
military.note: Reported military-controlled urban centre. The wider region includes resistance and contested areas; this is not a region-wide control boundary.

actors.name: NUG / PDFs and resistance forces
actors.note: The National Unity Government and many People’s Defence Forces cooperate with several ethnic armed organisations. They are not one army with a single chain of command; local alliances and control vary.

actors.name: Arakan Army / ULA
actors.note: An ethnic armed administration centred on Rakhine, pursuing its own political aims. Membership of an anti-military alliance does not mean subordination to the NUG.

actors.name: Kachin Independence Organisation / Army
actors.note: An ethnic armed organisation with its own administration and command, cooperating with parts of the wider resistance.

actors.name: Karen and Karenni organisations
actors.note: KNU/KNLA, Karenni organisations and local defence forces have distinct leaderships and partnerships. Their operations are not equivalent to full control of every township where they are active.

actors.name: MNDAA, TNLA, SSPP and RCSS
actors.note: Shan State contains several separate armed actors. Some have ceasefire arrangements, some oppose the military, and relationships change. They should not all be coloured as one resistance bloc.

actors.name: Military-aligned militias
actors.note: Groups such as the PNA, Pyu Saw Htee and SNA have military-aligned relationships. They are different from the ceasefire administrations in Wa and Mongla.

territoryDate: Boundary effective date unspecified; source snapshot 18 October 2026

nationalAssessment.note: ISP-Myanmar retrospective assessment for 2025. This is not a current territorial-control percentage and does not mean the other 62% was uniformly military-controlled.

coverage: Three approximate stable ceasefire-territory polygons and three dated urban military-centre markers. Areas without a classified polygon are unclassified or mixed, not automatically military-controlled. Other armed actors are described without inventing frontlines. Formal self-administered areas are a separate administrative reference.
